title: Erdős Problem #1011: Triangles in Graphs with High Chromatic Number
description: Let f_r(n) be minimal such that every n-vertex graph with ≥ f_r(n) edges and χ ≥ r contains a triangle. Known: f_2(n) = ⌊n²/4⌋+1 (Turán), f_3(n) = ⌊(n-1)²/4⌋+2 (Erdős-Gallai). Asymptotic involves g(r) ~ r² log r. OPEN.

meta.author: Erdős, Simonovits

overview.historicalContext:
Erdős Problem #1011 connects three fundamental graph invariants: edge count, chromatic number, and triangle existence. The threshold function f_r(n) gives the minimum number of edges such that every n-vertex graph with at least f_r(n) edges and chromatic number ≥ r must contain a triangle. Turán's theorem (1941) solved the case r=2: f_2(n) = ⌊n²/4⌋ + 1.

Erdős and Gallai (1962) determined f_3(n) = ⌊(n-1)²/4⌋ + 2, and Simonovits established the general asymptotic form f_r(n) = n²/4 - g(r)·n/2 + O(1) in his PhD thesis. Here g(r) measures how far triangle-free graphs with chromatic number ≥ r can be from bipartite. The problem thus reduces to understanding g(r).

Recent progress has narrowed the bounds significantly. Davies and Illingworth (2022) proved g(r) ≥ (1/2 - o(1))r² log r using χ-Ramsey techniques, while Hefty, Horn, King, and Pfender (2025) showed g(r) ≤ (2 + o(1))r² log r, building on advances in off-diagonal Ramsey numbers R(3,k). The factor-of-4 gap between these bounds remains open. Ren, Wang, Wang, and Yang (2024) recently determined the exact value f_4(n) for n ≥ 150.
overview.problemStatement: Let f_r(n) be minimal such that every graph on n vertices with at least f_r(n) edges and chromatic number at least r contains a triangle. Determine f_r(n).
overview.text: Let f_r(n) be minimal such that every n-vertex graph with ≥ f_r(n) edges and χ ≥ r contains a triangle. Known: f_2(n) = ⌊n²/4⌋+1 (Turán), f_3(n) = ⌊(n-1)²/4⌋+2 (Erdős-Gallai). Asymptotic involves g(r) ~ r² log r. OPEN.
overview.proofStrategy: The Lean formalization defines f_r(n) as a threshold function on graphs with chromatic number constraints. Known exact values for r=2,3,4 are stated as axioms. The Simonovits asymptotic f_r(n) = n²/4 - g(r)n/2 + O(1) introduces the key quantity g(r). Bounds on g(r) capture current knowledge: (1/2)r² log r ≤ g(r) ≤ 2r² log r.
keyInsights: Simonovits asymptotic: f_r(n) = n²/4 - g(r)n/2 + O(1)
g(r) = max vertices to remove from χ≥r triangle-free graph to make bipartite
Bounds: (1/2-o(1))r² log r ≤ g(r) ≤ (2+o(1))r² log r

conclusion.summary: The threshold f_r(n) for forcing triangles in graphs with chromatic number ≥ r is well-understood for small r but the general asymptotic remains open. Simonovits showed f_r(n) = n²/4 - g(r)n/2 + O(1) where g(r) captures how far triangle-free χ≥r graphs are from bipartite. Current bounds show g(r) ~ r² log r with a factor-of-4 gap in the constant.
conclusion.implications:
**Theoretical Significance**: This connects extremal graph theory (Turán-type problems) with chromatic theory.

Understanding g(r) would reveal how chromatic number constrains triangle-free graphs. The recent progress on R(3,k) (the Ramsey number) directly impacts the upper bound on g(r).
openQuestions: What is the exact constant c such that g(r) ~ c·r² log r?
What is f_5(n)? Higher exact values unknown.
Can Simonovits's O(1) error be made explicit?

crossReferences.description: Off-diagonal Ramsey numbers R(3,k) directly impact the upper bound on g(r); recent progress on R(3,k) by Campos et al. is what enables the HHKP upper bound g(r) ≤ (2+o(1))r² log r.
Erdős Problem #1009 also concerns triangles and chromatic number in extremal graph theory, sharing the Turán-type framework and the role of bipartite graphs as extremal constructions.
Erdős Problem #1010 is a companion extremal problem on triangle-free graphs with high chromatic number, directly feeding into the quantity g(r) central to Problem #1011.
Erdős Problem #1012 explores further Turán-type thresholds for subgraph containment, forming part of the same extremal graph theory program as Problem #1011.
Erdős Problem #500 on chromatic number and subgraph structure shares the core tension between local sparsity (triangle-free) and global complexity (high chromatic number).
Szemerédi's Regularity Lemma is the principal tool in proving asymptotic Turán-type results; the Simonovits asymptotic for f_r(n) relies on regularity-based graph decompositions.
